title: DeepSeek-V3.1 (Chat/Hybrid)
name: DeepSeek-V3.1 (Chat/Hybrid)
description: DeepSeek-V3.1 (Chat/Hybrid) is the family’s operationally flexible variant: one checkpoint with both thinking and non-thinking modes, plus stronger tool calling and agent behavior than the prior V3 generation.

best_for: Production chat systems that need both standard and reasoning paths in one variant.
Agent workloads with tool use and multi-step search or code tasks.
Mixed-quality/performance deployments where you want better price-performance than a reasoning-only model for routine traffic.
avoid_for: Environments that require fully published internal dimensions before approval.
Workloads that need a pure reasoning-only model and can tolerate less chat flexibility.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Use as the default DeepSeek deployment when the application needs both chat latency and selective thinking-mode capability without moving to a reasoning-only endpoint.
deployment_risks: Multi-node serving interconnect bottlenecks due to frontier-scale MoE model parameters.
State alignment issues when switching context dynamics between thinking and non-thinking modes under high concurrency.
failure_modes: Tokenizer/chat template parsing mismatch when serving V3.1 with legacy V3 configurations.
Expert Parallel scheduling imbalance or network all-reduce bottlenecks on cluster topologies.
common_mistakes: Treating V3.1 as a generic chat model, bypassing the think/non-think template controls.
Attempting single-GPU serving without planning high-speed interconnect and sharded tensor parallelism.
operational_notes: V3.1’s main operational difference is mode switching: the same model supports both thinking and non-thinking behavior, and vLLM exposes that as a per-request toggle.
The official vLLM recipe recommends an 8xH200 or H20 multi-GPU serving setup, which makes the full checkpoint a multi-node or high-end single-node deployment problem rather than a workstation model.
The model card states training with UE8M0 FP8 scale data format on weights and activations, which makes FP8-capable serving infrastructure especially relevant.
DeepSeek V3.1 uses an updated tokenizer and chat template; the official release note explicitly points to the tokenizer config, so integrations should not assume the V3 template is drop-in identical.

Variant differentiation (Identity): DeepSeek-V3.1 (Chat/Hybrid) is the family’s operationally flexible variant: one checkpoint with both thinking and non-thinking modes, plus stronger tool calling and agent behavior than the prior V3 generation.
Variant differentiation (File Formats): GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ and Apple Silicon MLX/ONNX formats are Not Published in retrieved resources, indicating server-centric GPU focus.
Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): vLLM’s official recipe shows serving on 8xH200 or H20 GPUs (141GB × 8) as the baseline for the full checkpoint.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): canonical downloads are Hugging Face checkpoints for V3.1 base and instruct weights, alongside API updates.
Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): vLLM recipes explicitly support dynamic think/non-think toggles, whereas edge runtimes (llama.cpp) are undocumented.
Variant differentiation (Deployment): hybrid think/non-think serving gives V3.1 flexible deployment latency options relative to reasoning-only variants like R1-0528.
Variant differentiation (License): MIT License allows very broad open-source utilization including modification, redistribution, and commercial deployment without active constraints.
Variant differentiation (Status): officially released production checkpoint targeted at robust structured reasoning.
